subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs default to delete-after-run session cleanup, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as one-shot-only behavior?
rationale: Two open PRs choose conflicting lifecycle contracts, and either direction affects existing cron jobs, future defaults, and session-state cleanup semantics.

options.title: Adopt recurring cleanup default
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, add upgrade/load or doctor coverage for existing omitted isolated jobs, and reconcile the one-shot-only PR against that contract.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only validation
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the stricter validation path after caller, UI, and upgrade recovery gaps are resolved.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Land the default as-is while explicitly documenting that existing omitted jobs require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Adopt recurring cleanup default
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, add upgrade/load or doctor coverage for existing omitted isolated jobs, and reconcile the one-shot-only PR against that contract.
